subject: FastTrack latency surge + product trade-off questions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-oncall@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Jul 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: FastTrack: P99 latency spike on embeddings-gen-service (detected)

Team —

Monitoring just alerted: p99 for embeddings-gen-service (model: embed-8b-quant) jumped from ~220ms to ~2.1s at 08:07 PDT for FastTrack production traffic. Error rates are stable (no 5xx spike), but we see a large tail on token streaming and a concurrent increase in average NVMe wait on the host.

First-pass notes:
- Scope: ~12% of FastTrack requests in last 5m see >1s latency, mostly long-context churn (session length >2k tokens).
- Recent infra change: rolling kernel update last night (kernel 5.15 -> 5.16) and a model quantization rollout to embed-8b-quant yesterday (canary -> 60% traffic).
- Immediate suspect: IO pressure + kv-cache misses when models load new segments.

Attaching a 1-min spike graph and last 200 log lines (tail) for quick triage. Im spinning up an extra pool with older quantized binary to route a small percentage for mitigation.

Action asks to start:
1) Product: can we temporarily route FastTrack to embed-8b-fp16 (smaller qps cost, verified quality delta) while we stabilize? estimated impact on cost/quality?
2) Infra/SRE: confirm whether the kernel roll triggered any NVMe driver regressions and whether we can fallback hosts without impacting other tenants.
3) Eng: collect profile traces from a sample request (I started capture 08:10).

Ill update in 10m with mitigation status.

Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: p99_spike_graph.png (image/png), service-logs-tail.txt (text/plain)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Jul 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FastTrack: P99 latency spike on embeddings-gen-service (detected)

Thanks Ben —

Appreciate the quick triage. Quick alignment: Im going to coordinate the customer message (short, honest, no technical noise) and loop in Product and Eng for trade-offs. Proposed plan below; please flag if any item is risky.

Proposed internal plan (next 60m):
- SRE: keep the extra pool routing live at 10% traffic to measure impact (Ben).
- Eng: continue trace capture; if we confirm kv-cache cold misses are primary, consider temporarily increasing cache prewarm for affected sessions (Karthik).
- Product: evaluate short-term fallback to embed-8b-fp16 for FastTrack only (Marissa) — need impact on similarity precision and billing delta.
- Customer comm: send below draft to Alex at FastTrack now, mark as "update" not "root cause".

Draft to customer (please review/edit quickly):
---
Subject: Update on todays latency increase

Hi Alex —

We detected an increase in response latency affecting a portion of your requests this morning. Our SRE team is actively mitigating and weve routed a subset of your traffic to a fallback model to reduce the impact while we investigate. We expect to have more detailed findings within 2 hours and will share a follow-up with root cause and long-term mitigations.

Sorry for the disruption — were prioritizing this.

Best,
Stephanie
---

Marissa/Karthik: if you can reply-all with product/technical guidance Ill hold on sending until I get your OK (aiming <08:40).

-Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: product-eng@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Jul 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FastTrack: P99 latency spike on embeddings-gen-service (detected)

Thanks Steph / Ben —

A few product-side constraints and asks before we send anything that mentions fallbacks:
1) Quality delta: we have A/B evals comparing embed-8b-quant -> embed-8b-fp16. Expected precision drop for semantic-similarity >= 0.9 for short contexts but can degrade up to 0.04 MAP for long-context aggregation. For FastTracks use-case (chat history + retrieval, many long contexts) this might be measurable. If we route only 10% for now, can we A/B monitor requests and auto-escalate to 25% if quality stays within threshold?
2) Billing: fp16 payload increases average token compute cost by ~15% for the routed traffic. We should decide if Redwood absorbs this as a one-off SLA credit or pass-through. Recommend: Redwood absorb for the next 2 hours while we stabilize.
3) Roadmap question: were already prioritized a KV-cache prewarm change in Q4. If kv-cache cold-starts are the cause, can we accelerate a limited scope prewarm toggle for the FastTrack tenancy? Engineering ETA?

Actionable asks:
- Karthik: can Eng provide ETA for a prewarm toggle (minutes/hours)?
- Ben: if you confirm kernel/driver regression, do we have a safe host rollback plan that doesnt evict other customers?
- Steph: hold sending external note until we confirm A/B plan and credit decision (Im fine with a short 10% mitigation window if we monitor quality).

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Lead, Serving & Reliability

From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@fasttrack.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Jul 2028 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Update on today’s latency increase

Thanks for the quick note, Stephanie. Appreciate you routing a portion of traffic and keeping us updated. Two quick asks from our side: 1) will observable outputs (similarity scores) change for routed requests — we rely on a deterministic similarity threshold; 2) can you give us an ETA (rough) for the full mitigation or a more detailed follow-up so we can sync internal CS/engineering?

Were keeping non-critical indexing jobs paused until we get the follow-up. If theres anything you want us to run or sample on our side (request ids, example payloads), tell us and well share.

—Alex
Alex Porter
Head of ML Infrastructure, FastTrack

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-oncall@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FastTrack: P99 latency spike on embeddings-gen-service (detected)

Update — mitigation in progress.

What weve done (08:12-10:00):
- Routed 10% of FastTrack traffic to embed-8b-fp16 at 08:18; p99 for routed subset dropped to ~280ms within 3m.
- Opened isolated pool with pre-roll binaries (no kernel change) and moved 30% of FastTrack traffic there at 09:05 — p99 for that pool: ~320ms.
- Captured traces for 1.2k requests; preliminary signal: ~72% of slow requests show extended NVMe wait during kv-cache population. No clear evidence of a model runtime regression.
- Started rolling host rollback for the smallest set of affected hosts (manual; no eviction) at 09:45.

Answers to product/customer asks:
- Observable scores: fp16 route shows <0.03 average cosine delta vs quantized baseline for short-contexts, larger variance for multi-thousand-token aggregation. Recommend we continue A/B at 10% and collect similarity score histograms to answer Alex's deterministic threshold question.
- ETA: We expect stabilization (p99 < 350ms for >90% traffic) within 2 hours if NVMe pressure subsides after rollback and pool routing. If kernel driver rollback is required more widely the timeline may extend.

I attached the spike graph and the logs tail for your review. Im moving to a short war-room; please add any additional questions here.

Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: p99_spike_graph.png, service-logs-tail.txt, runbook-mitigation.md
